record.title: Council of Europe bureau discusses draft privacy guidance for LLM systems and agents
record.summary: The Council of Europe’s Convention 108 Bureau reported that its 66th meeting in Paris on September 16–17, 2026 discussed draft guidelines on data protection in LLM-based systems, including agentic systems, with a view to finalization and adoption during 2026 and no later than the June 2027 plenary. The August 26 draft frames itself as interpretive guidance for existing Convention 108+ duties; it says it creates no new rights or obligations and does not prescribe specific technologies. The guidelines have not been shown as adopted in the inspected sources.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Council of Europe published a draft titled Draft Guidelines on Privacy and Data Protection in the context of LLM-based systems, dated August 26, 2026. The draft covers processing through LLM and LLM-based system lifecycles, including AI agents and agentic systems where Convention 108+ applies.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Council of Europe reports that the Bureau’s 66th meeting in Paris on September 16–17 discussed draft data-protection guidelines for LLMs and neurosciences, with a view to finalization and adoption during 2026 and no later than the plenary meeting in June 2027.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The August 26 LLM draft says it is interpretive, does not create new rights or additional obligations under Convention 108+, and does not prescribe a specific technology, architecture or organizational arrangement. The inspected material does not establish formal adoption.

evidence_gaps.description: The inspected Council of Europe page records a draft and an intended adoption window but does not establish whether a finalized version has since been adopted.

brief.importance_rationale: If finalized and applied as described, this cross-lifecycle interpretation of Convention 108+ for LLM and agentic systems could inform privacy and data-governance decisions across European organizations and public authorities. Score 4 reflects meaningful policy and implementation relevance; the document remains a draft, expressly adds no new obligations, and has not been shown as adopted.
limitations: The Bureau report and linked document establish discussion of a draft, not formal adoption or implementation.
The draft expressly says it is interpretive, creates no new rights or obligations under Convention 108+, and does not prescribe specific technical measures.
The stated target was adoption during 2026 and no later than the June 2027 plenary; no later adoption status was established in this activation.
The ANPD Portuguese article was published on October 26 but reports the September meeting; it is not evidence of a new October legal action.

technical.claimed_result: The draft is intended to support interpretation and practical implementation of existing Convention 108+ data-protection principles for LLM-based systems, including agents.
technical.demonstrated_result: An official August 26 draft and September 17 Bureau meeting report are publicly available; the Bureau report records discussion and a planned adoption timeline.
technical.implementation_status: Draft discussed by the Bureau on September 16–17, 2026; finalization/adoption was targeted during 2026 and no later than the June 2027 plenary. Formal adoption and implementation were not verified.
technical.mechanism: The Consultative Committee is preparing interpretive, principles-based guidance for applying Convention 108+ across the LLM processing lifecycle, with a separate section on agentic LLM-based systems.
technical.regime: Council of Europe Convention 108+ data-protection guidance for LLM-based systems, including agentic systems where the Convention applies.
technical.reproducibility: This is a policy-process record verified against official Council of Europe materials and an original-language ANPD account; no independent legal interpretation or implementation outcome was assessed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Existing Convention 108+ principles and obligations; the draft states it adds no rights or obligations beyond them.

brief.title: Council of Europe bureau discusses draft privacy guidance for LLM systems and agents
brief.why_it_matters: The draft applies existing data-protection principles across LLM development and operation, including system integration, retrieval, memory, tools, agent communications and operational records. If finalized, it could help organizations interpret privacy duties for agentic systems. Its current draft status and express non-creation of new obligations are central limits.
